subject: four NOI inputs to verify
preheader: inconsistent income and expense assumptions can overstate a screen.
headline: A useful NOI comparison needs consistent inputs.
body: Check 1: vacancy. A pro forma that assumes full collection may omit turnover and credit loss. For illustration, an entered 8% vacancy assumption on $1,800 monthly rent is $1,728 per year; 8% is an example, not a universal benchmark.

Check 2: management. Use the proposed management scope and fee when applicable. If you self-manage, a zero cash fee may match the accounting convention, but it does not measure your time or prove the property is easier to operate.
Check 3: effective income. Keep gross scheduled rent, vacancy, concessions, and other income distinct so two cap-rate comparisons use the same convention.

Check 4: capital work. TrueCap treats the CapEx reserve below NOI under its disclosed convention, while modeled cash flow still subtracts it. Review roof, HVAC, water heater, appliance, and other condition evidence instead of importing a universal reserve percentage.
The NOI guide below walks through each input so you can review the math before running the full property in TrueCap.
